page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor cores operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 93.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, equipped with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core CPU performance and GPU-assisted or multi-threaded workloads. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, fall into the weak category, while single-threaded gzip compression is poor. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks consistently rank in the average tier. The standout capability of this hardware configuration lies in LLM inference. Prompt processing speeds for both small and medium models achieve top-tier status, and text generation for medium models is rated as strong.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the overhead of high-end tensor core GPUs. The primary tradeoff is the lower single-core CPU performance and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external block storage solutions. This profile makes the instance highly suitable for workloads such as medium-scale LLM inference, ray tracing, image processing, and multi-threaded database operations, whereas it is less optimal for single-threaded processing tasks.
